name: endurance
description: Maximum lifetime profile. Huge over-provisioning, static pSLC region, aggressive wear leveling, conservative NAND timing. For drives that need to live a long time under constant write load (e.g. a log/cache/scratch drive, a long-running swap device, a 24/7 recorder). Trades substantial capacity for 3-5× factory lifetime.

capacity_impact.method: usable ≈ advertised × (1 − OP/100) × (1 − pSLC/100). Big OP + static pSLC = big capacity haircut.

host_recommendations.filesystem: ext4 with low journaling, or no filesystem for raw log use
notes: Expect ~3-5× the P/E cycle lifetime of a factory-tuned drive, due to the larger spare pool spreading wear evenly.
pSLC region (20%) is static, so always-fast writes go there and wear slower.
Thermal 60°C setpoint is cooler than default — NAND retention improves with lower junction temp.
This profile is overkill for 'occasional backup stick' use. It's for drives expected to see >100 TBW over their life.
